thread:
Kevin: heads up — since the CNI rollout last night i'm seeing spikes in intra-cluster dns timeouts, svc->svc calls intermittently failing with gRPC deadline exceeded. started ~02:10 UTC. logs show lots of truncated UDP responses (TC bit) and then long delays while clients fall back to TCP.

Sophie: ouch. are these coming from node-local-dns or CoreDNS?

Kevin: primarily node-local-dns on the GPU pools. node-local forwarder is getting SERVFAIL / truncated replies to CoreDNS, then clients hang for ~200-800ms before retry over tcp. packet capture on node shows DNS UDP fragments and occasional ip fragment reassembly failures.

Mari: did the CNI change the MTU or enable encapsulation? last deploy set "encap: vxlan" on some subnets.

Kevin: yep — vxlan on east-west across AZ2. MTU mismatch between hosts + downstream physical switches clamping to 1500. some nodes have iface mtu 9000, others 1500. results in fragmentation.

Raj: that explains the TC (truncated) — DNS over UDP with large EDNS0 payloads gets fragmented and the fragments are dropped. CoreDNS isn't at fault, it's the network path.

Kevin: here's a quick excerpt from tcpdump on a node (redacted):
```
18:22:39.123456 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 54321, offset 0, flags [DF]) 10.0.4.12.53123 > 10.0.0.5.53: UDP, length 1452
18:22:39.123457 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 54322, offset 1480, flags [none]) 10.0.4.12 > 10.0.0.5: frag (1480)
18:22:39.123459 IP 10.0.4.12.53123 > 10.0.0.5.53: UDP, length 2048
```
and node-local-dns logs: "failed to reassemble fragments: packet too small / short read"

Sophie: any quick mitigations we can do while infra patches MTU? can we reduce EDNS0 reply sizes or force dns over tcp fallback faster?

Raj: short-term options:
- reduce EDNS0 UDP size at CoreDNS (eg set edns0size 512)
- disable EDNS0 on the node-local-dns forwarder if possible
- reduce the DNS response size by trimming records (not ideal)
- configure kubelet/resolv.conf to prefer TCP? (no native knob, client libs handle that)

Mari: can we roll a config change in CoreDNS to set edns0size 512 and bump the node-local-dns restart? Shouldn't break clients.

Kevin: i'm preparing a canary patch to CoreDNS to set edns0size 512 and a configmap change for node-local-dns to limit UDP response sizes. will roll to a small subset of GPU nodes first.

Oncall-SRE: tagging @infra oncall. Also, I'm seeing svc mesh health degrade — 100ms p95 increase on a few internal APIs. please escalate if degradation continues.

infra-bot: deploy-triggered: coredns-config-change -> started (canary: gpu-pool-1). CI: ✅  Unit tests for coredns-config.

Sophie: also let's add a monitoring alert for "dns.tc_rate > 0.5%" — surfaced as high TCP fallback rate. want a graph for cluster and per-node breakdown.

Raj: long-term we should ensure MTU consistency: either standardize on 1500 across hosts, or enable path MTU discovery through the overlay (and validate switch configs). also add fragmentation metrics at the node egress.

Kevin: roll completed on canary — node-local-dns pods restarted. early signs: tcp fallback reduced, SERVFAIL down to baseline. still seeing a handful of nodes with continued failures.

Mari: i'm running a quick ansible job to reconcile MTU on GPU nodes to 1500 across the board and disabling jumbo on ENIs in the misconfigured AZ. will report back in 15m.

Kevin: detected one oddity — some of the RDMA-enabled hosts had MTU 9000 and are using SR-IOV passthrough; touching those requires a scheduled maintenance window. not touching RDMA hosts in this patch.

Sophie: good call. avoid touching RDMA until we coordinate. can we add an interim nginx health-probe retry in front of grpc clients to hide transient DNS spikes?

Raj: we can also reduce client DNS TTL reliance — increase kube-dns config to cache negative/positive answers longer, but that trades staleness for availability.

infra-bot: alert: dns-truncation-rate spiked to 3.2% at 02:18 UTC — now down to 0.4% post-canary.

Oncall-SRE: next steps list:
- finish MTU reconciliation (Mari)
- audit CNI encap/mtu defaults and document (Raj)
- add dns truncation and tcp-fallback dashboards (Sophie)
- schedule RDMA host maintenance separately (Kevin + infra)
- follow up on node-local-dns config to hard-limit EDNS0 (Kevin)

Mari: MTU job finished on 12/18 nodes in GPU pool, failures correlated to 4 remaining RDMA-capable hosts.

Kevin: metrics look much better cluster-wide. leaving thread open for the RDMA windows and post-maintenance validation. thanks all :thumbsup:

Sophie: nice work team. adding retro note to incident board and a short runbook for future encap/mtu rollouts.

Raj: filing a small infra PR to add an MTU check to our preflight CI for CNI rollouts.

infra-bot: incident-ops: created postmortem draft #463: "dns-truncation-after-vxlan-rollout"

Kevin: closing when RDMA hosts validated, will update timestamps in the postmortem.

Oncall-SRE: acknowledged.
